deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a page of Riemann's student essay 'Versuch einer allgemeinen Auffassung der Integration und Differentiation' (1847). It was published posthumously in the Gesammelte Werke (1876). The previous pages define the generalized derivative ∂_x^ν z for arbitrary real ν. The general value is a particular value plus a complementary function C^ν, so it is enough to find one value. For negative ν that value is the integral (Ausdruck 1) ∂_x^ν z = 1/Π(-ν-1) ∫_k^x (x-t)^{-ν-1} z(t) dt, where Π(s)=Γ(s+1).

(a) Programme. To compute derivatives of particular functions one need only find one value. The general value then follows by adding C. For the transformation of Ausdruck 1 to be useful, this value should be simpler than the integral, i.e. an explicit function of x in finite form. In practice this means getting x out from under the integral sign.

(b) Example z = x^μ. For μ positive, x^μ is continuous for all x (including 0). So with lower limit 0, the expression 1/Π(-ν-1) ∫_0^x (x-t)^{-ν-1} t^μ dt is a value of ∂_x^ν(x^μ).

The substitution t = x y (my explicit statement; it is implicit in the footnote #) gives
∫_0^x (x-t)^{-ν-1} t^μ dt = x^{μ-ν} ∫_0^1 (1-y)^{-ν-1} y^μ dy = x^{μ-ν} B(μ+1, -ν) = x^{μ-ν} Γ(μ+1)Γ(-ν)/Γ(μ-ν+1).
Dividing by Π(-ν-1) = Γ(-ν) yields ∂_x^ν(x^μ) = Π(μ)/Π(μ-ν) · x^{μ-ν}. This is the footnote # line.

(c) Extension to arbitrary order. The m-th ordinary derivative of Π(μ)/Π(μ-ν) x^{μ-ν} is Π(μ)/Π(μ-ν-m) x^{μ-ν-m}. By property [1] (d^m/dx^m ∂^ν = ∂^{ν+m}), this is a value of ∂_x^{ν+m}(x^μ). Since every order can be written ν+m with ν<0 and m a natural number, for every ν one has
∂_x^ν(x^μ) = Π(μ)/Π(μ-ν) · x^{μ-ν} + C^ν.

The red marginalia (𝔇_x^ν(x^μ), ∂_x^ν(x^μ), 'besondere Zeile') are later editorial or printer's marks about notation and layout.
errors: The first written integrand in the line (with (x-t)^{μ-ν-1}(t-y)^{-ν-1} y^μ dy) is garbled and is struck out. It is replaced by the correct footnote #: ∫_0^1 x^{μ-ν}(1-y)^{-ν-1} y^μ dy.

Unstated convergence conditions: the integral requires ν<0 (i.e. -ν>0) at the upper end and μ>-1 at the lower end. 'μ positive' is sufficient but stronger than needed. The ν<0 restriction is implicit and is what makes step (c) necessary.

Step (c) relies on the earlier property [1] that ordinary differentiation composes additively with ∂^ν (modulo complementary functions). It is assumed rather than reproved here; this is fine in context.
The final formula is singular or degenerate when μ-ν is a negative integer (1/Π(μ-ν)=0). This is not discussed, though it is consistent with the C-function framework.

results.what: ∂_x^ν x^μ = Γ(μ+1)/Γ(μ-ν+1) x^{μ-ν} via the Riemann–Liouville integral with lower limit 0, using the Beta integral
results.modern_name: Riemann–Liouville fractional derivative/integral of a power function

results.what: Extension from negative to arbitrary order by composing with ordinary derivatives, with the general value given up to the complementary function C^ν
results.modern_name: Riemann–Liouville derivative D^ν = D^m I^{m-ν}; Riemann's complementary function

deep.surprise_reason: This page is part of Riemann's 1847 'Versuch', published in his Werke (1876). The power-function formula is the standard textbook example of Riemann–Liouville fractional calculus and is well known as his.

checkable.asserts: Beta integral evaluation (expected 0 for mu>-1, nu<0)
Half-integral (nu=-1/2) of x^2 equals Π(2)/Π(5/2) x^{5/2}
The m-th derivative (m=3) of Π(μ)/Π(μ-ν) x^{μ-ν} is Π(μ)/Π(μ-ν-m) x^{μ-ν-m}

transcription_corrections: 'der sich aus 6[?] dessen' — the '6' appears to be a stray stroke; the reading is 'der sich aus dessen ...' (or similar).
'+ Cν' should be read as '+ C^ν' (the complementary function of order ν).
The struck-out text in the integral line is the garbled first attempt; the valid evaluation is the footnote # with ∫_0^1 x^{μ-ν}(1-y)^{-ν-1}y^μ dy.
'mte Differentialhiervon' should read 'das mte Differential hiervon'.
